tech.heading: Currently using
tech.description: Not a complete stack list, but the tools I keep reaching for while connecting research, product work, and personal systems.

typescript.description: My default for product prototypes, frontend state, and maintainable system boundaries.

react.description: Used for interaction-heavy tools, product surfaces, and experimental interfaces.

rust.description: Useful for local performance, desktop apps, and system parts that need firm boundaries.

next.description: A good fit when content, product experience, and server-side capability meet.

node.description: The everyday runtime for APIs, scripts, data handling, and fast engineering prototypes.

docker.description: Keeps research environments, service dependencies, and deployment paths reproducible.

vue.description: A comfortable UI layer for content systems and lightweight interaction work.

nuxt.description: The framework behind this site, handling content, localization, and page experience.

javascript.description: Still the fastest base for browser experiments, small tools, and quick idea checks.

expo.description: One of the fastest paths into mobile AI workflows and cross-platform prototypes.

tauri.description: A lightweight shell for local-first desktop tools and local AI pipelines.

zotero.description: Core infrastructure for reading, citation management, and long-term research memory.

obsidian.description: A workspace for personal knowledge, project notes, and long-term memory systems.

cplusplus.description: Still important for local AI, audio/video work, and performance-sensitive modules.

turborepo.description: Helps keep multi-app and multi-package prototypes moving together.

tailwind.description: Lets interface work move quickly while keeping tool surfaces consistent.

gitea.description: Self-hostable code and collaboration infrastructure for long-lived personal systems.

vite.description: Keeps frontend experiments and component prototypes close to instant.

electron.description: Still practical when mature desktop capability and a web stack need to meet.

reactNative.description: Connects mobile interaction, capture flows, and personal workflow prototypes.

vscode.description: My main editor for daily engineering, AI-assisted development, and research code.

xcode.description: Used for iOS prototypes, device debugging, and validating mobile interaction details.

postman.description: Useful for API checks, service boundaries, and keeping interface workflows clear.
